subject: Logic
title: Beyond Propositions
description: A short lesson to help you apply Beyond Propositions.

hook.text: "All dogs are loyal" can't be expressed with P and Q alone. You need a more powerful language.

buildup.text: Propositional logic treats whole statements as atoms. Predicate logic looks inside—at subjects and properties.

discovery.text: "D(x)" means "x is a dog." "L(x)" means "x is loyal." Now you can write: for all x, D(x) → L(x).

twist.text: This jump from propositional to predicate logic was one of the biggest leaps in the history of reasoning.

climax.text: Predicate logic can express relationships, quantities, and structures that propositional logic simply cannot.

quiz.question: What does predicate logic add beyond propositional logic?
